summary: This document fixes minor issues found in the Opus audio codec as specified in RFC 6716. It updates the normative decoder implementation in that RFC's Appendix A, addressing real and potential security-related problems and some small quality issues.

plainLanguage.summary: It is a patch for a sound-compression recipe. A few small mistakes were found and corrected so the music and voices come out right and safely.

questions: what changed in the opus codec
subtitle: A patch set for the Opus reference decoder: security fixes, small quality fixes and new test vectors.

tldr.problem: The reference decoder in Appendix A of RFC 6716 had real and potential security-related bugs, plus a few minor quality problems. Opus is defined by that decoder code, so the code itself had to be corrected.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists code patches for the decoder: stereo state reset, padding parsing, the resampler buffer, two integer wrap-arounds, a cap on band energy, hybrid folding and an optional mono downmix tweak. It also adds new test vectors.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 6716 and stays fully compatible with it. Two CVEs are fixed, and new implementations SHOULD be based on the new test vectors.

today: RFC 8251 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6716 and has not been updated or obsoleted itself. New Opus implementations should follow the updated decoder behavior and test vectors.

sections.title: Why the Decoder Needed Patches
sections.content:
Unlike most IETF specifications, RFC 6716 defines the Opus codec through a normative reference decoder implementation (Appendix A) rather than through the accompanying text. That is why this document only lists issues in the decoder: the code is the specification.

Some of the changes alter normative behavior in a way that needs new test vectors. Only the C implementation is affected, not the English text of the specification, and the result remains fully compatible with RFC 6716. The patches are printed in the RFC as code diffs, with approximate line numbers.
sections.plainLanguage: The recipe book for Opus is really a working example kitchen. When bugs were found in that kitchen, the fix had to be written as changes to the kitchen itself.

sections.title: Packet Padding Overflow
sections.content:
Some invalid packets of a very large size could trigger an out-of-bounds read in the code that parses Opus packet padding. The cause is an integer overflow when the signaled padding exceeds 2^31-1 bytes, even if the actual packet is smaller.

The fix decrements the signed len value directly instead of adding up a separate padding counter. The RFC says the read reaches up to about 60 KB beyond the compressed buffer and needs a packet more than about 16 MB long, so it is not a problem for RTP. In theory it could crash a file decoder such as Opus in Ogg, but the authors' attempts to trigger a crash in a production application failed.
sections.plainLanguage: A note on the package could claim a huge amount of packing paper, and the counter for it got confused. Now the decoder just subtracts from what is left, so it cannot lose track.

sections.title: Resampler Buffer Fixes
sections.content:
The SILK resampler had three problems. The calls to memcpy() used sizeof(opus_int32) although the local buffer holds opus_int16 values. Because the size was wrong, the source and destination of one copy could overlap. And the buffer was sized with RESAMPLER_MAX_BATCH_SIZE_IN, but the data stored in it was actually twice the input batch size.

The patch doubles the buffer size, uses opus_int16 in the size calculations and switches the overlapping copy from buf to buf to silk_memmove. The authors believe the overlap would not be a problem once the type size is fixed, since the input sample count is at least the sampling rate in kHz, which is at least 8, and RESAMPLER_ORDER_FIR_12 is only 8.
sections.plainLanguage: The decoder measured a box with the wrong ruler and also bought a box that was too small. The fix uses the right ruler and a bigger box.

sections.title: Integer Wrap-Around Fixes
sections.content:
Two bugs were found by decoder fuzzing (feeding the decoder unusual bitstreams). In LPC_inverse_pred_gain_QA(), some bitstreams produced values exceeding 32 bits, causing a wrap-around that the C standard treats as undefined behavior. The patch detects values that do not fit in a 32-bit integer and treats the corresponding filter as unstable.

In the Line Spectral Frequency (LSF) decoding, extremely large values for the high LSF parameters could wrap around and lead to an illegal read access on the stack. The authors do not believe it is exploitable, but fix it anyway by using a saturating 16-bit addition, silk_ADD_SAT16.
sections.plainLanguage: It is like an odometer that rolls over from the highest number back to zero. The fix makes the counter stop at the top instead of rolling over to a nonsense number.

sections.title: Quality Fixes and the Mono Downmix Option
sections.content:
Four smaller changes improve audio rather than safety. On a mode switch the SILK stereo state was not reset, which could produce a brief single-sample impulse; the patch clears it. In the CELT part, log-domain band energies could exceed the maximum single-precision float on extreme bitstreams and produce NaN (not a number) output; the patch caps the value.

Hybrid folding: at low bitrate in hybrid mode there may be enough bits for only one CELT band (8 - 9.6 kHz). The second band (CELT band 18, 9.6 - 12 kHz) then fell back to white noise, which could cause audible pre-echo. The fix repeats part of the first band when folding the second. The RFC says it does not impact compatibility.

Downmix to mono: Opus intensity stereo can code the two channels 180 degrees out of phase per band, which cancels energy when mixed down to mono. The decoder MAY choose not to apply the 180-degree phase shift. This is described as a work-around rather than a bug fix.
sections.plainLanguage: A few small tweaks make sound cleaner: no pops when switching modes, no broken numbers, no hiss in one frequency band, and no cancelled sound when stereo is squashed into one speaker.

sections.title: New Test Vectors
sections.content:
The hybrid folding and downmix changes affect decoder output enough to make the old test vectors fail, so the RFC provides new ones. Each bitstream now has two decoded outputs: files with suffix m do not apply the CELT 180-degree phase shift, and files without it do. The input .bit files are unchanged.

An implementation is compliant if it passes either the original vectors from RFC 6716 or one of the new sets. However, newer implementations SHOULD be based on the new vectors. The RFC lists SHA-1 hashes for testvector01 to testvector12.
sections.plainLanguage: The answer key for checking the decoder now has two correct versions of each answer. Matching either one earns full marks.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The document fixes two security issues in the RFC 6716 reference implementation. CVE-2013-0899 could theoretically have caused an information leak, with the leaked information passing through the decoder before reaching an attacker; the padding fix addresses it. CVE-2017-0381 could have resulted in a 16-bit out-of-bounds read from a fixed location; the LSF fix addresses it.

Beyond these two CVEs, the document adds no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 6716. It requires no IANA actions.
sections.plainLanguage: Two doors that a bad guy might have peeked through are now locked, and no new doors were added.

viz.caption: THE DECODER ISSUES FIXED IN RFC 8251

items.title: Stereo state
items.text: Reset on mode switch to avoid a one-sample impulse.

items.title: Padding
items.text: No overflow when parsing signaled padding.

items.title: Resampler
items.text: Correct buffer size, element size and copy.

items.title: Wrap-arounds
items.text: Inverse gain and LSF decoding no longer overflow.

items.title: Band energy
items.text: Capped so output cannot become NaN.

items.title: Hybrid folding
items.text: Second band no longer falls back to white noise.
